summary: A legatee in Ives's 1939 will, probably working-class and employed in the service sector - at the Spread Eagle Hotel, Midhurst, and latterly at 1 Greek Street, London W1 - whom Cook suggests was 'perhaps a former lover' of Ives.
certainty_reasoning: The only attestation is Cook's explicit speculation ('perhaps a former lover'), offered alongside his own competing non-sexual reading; the identification is credited by endnote to Brian Lewis by personal communication, with no archival citation. Classified uncorroborated - a lone, hedged allegation - with the competing reading recorded in the disputed block.

disputed.claim: That Charles French was a former lover of Ives.
disputed.asserted_by: Cook, in an explicitly hedged suggestion: 'French was perhaps a former lover'.
disputed.disputed_by: Cook himself, who immediately offers the competing reading that French was one of the men Ives called 'Ducks' - helped out intermittently but thought hopeless cases.
disputed.grounds: Cook's endnote 84 credits the connection to Brian Lewis by personal communication, with no archival citation.

sources.quote: Probably working-class, employed in the service sector (which we've already seen had a reputation for attracting queer men), French was perhaps a former lover, though was also one of the men Ives went on to call 'Ducks' (short for 'lame ducks' - men he helped out intermittently but thought hopeless cases).
sources.context: Cook, on a legatee named in Ives's 1939 will as having worked at the Spread Eagle Hotel, Midhurst, and latterly at 1 Greek Street, London W1
sources.supports: Charles French as a possible former lover of Ives - Cook's own speculation, offered alongside a competing non-sexual reading.
